To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the patients with small cell lung cancer who received chemotherapy followed by surgery have a good prognosis.

(1) 20 out of 142 patients (14%) with small cell carcinoma received surgery after systemic chemotherapy; (2) 18 of 20 patients were considered to be resectable; (3) 15 of 20 specimens showed small cell carcinoma pathologically, and three had non small cell carcinoma; (4) two patients survived for more five years; (5) the median survival was 22 months
the survival rate of the small cell lung cancer patients with resection after chemotherapy was better than that of patients with non-small cell lung cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the efficacy of chemotherapy in small cell carcinoma of lung; 2) the feasibility and efficacy of surgery after chemotherapy; and 3) the survival rate and the prognostic factors in patients with small cell lung cancer.
the development of a new method for the treatment of the lung.
the following points; 1) The efficacy of chemotherapy in patients with small cell lung cancer, and 2) The possibility of surgery in patients who respond to chemotherapy
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of surgical treatment in small cell carcinoma of lung has yet to be determined.
the role of surgery for small cell carcinoma of lung is limited to a few selected patients who have had a good response to systemic chemotherapy and are in good clinical condition.
the results of surgery after chemotherapy in patients with small cell lung cancer are not as encouraging as in non-small cell lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with limited stage disease who have achieved a good response to chemotherapy may be candidates for resection.

patients with small cell lung cancer who have received chemotherapy alone or chemotherapy and radiotherapy may have a chance to undergo resection, and the prognosis of these patients is better than that of the non-resected group.
surgery after chemotherapy is a feasible procedure for the treatment of small cell lung cancer, and that a longer survival time may be expected in patients with resectable disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients who are able to undergo surgery after chemotherapy for lung small cell cancer can have a very good prognosis.
patients with small cell lung cancer should be considered for surgical resection after chemotherapy if there is no evidence of metastatic disease.
the patients who had a complete response to chemotherapy and those with a partial response who had a resectable lesion after chemotherapy were the most likely to survive.
